security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG decodes the CHERI GCHI instruction using the old funct5=00000 encoding instead of the new funct5=10000 encoding, causing decode collision with SCBNDSI (Set Capability Bounds immediate). The decoder dispatches the wrong instruction for a given 32-bit opcode, so guest code assembled for one ISA version silently executes a semantically unrelated instruction under the other ISA version.
security_spec.summary: GCHI funct5 field changed from 0b00000 to 0b10000 to resolve an encoding clash with SCBNDSI; QEMU using stale decode tables would silently confuse a capability-bounds-setting instruction (SCBNDSI) with a capability-metadata-read instruction (GCHI), undermining CHERI capability confinement.

findings.finding: CHERI instruction decoding (GCHI, SCBNDSI) is not present in upstream QEMU. The vulnerability pattern describes a decode collision in CHERI-specific code that does not exist in this repository. The audit cannot confirm or deny the bug because the target code is absent — this is a CHERI-fork-only concern.
findings.snippet: N/A — no CHERI decode patterns found in target/riscv/insn32.decode or anywhere in the repo
